weeklyQuote: Richemont's jewellery sales prove shoppers still spend on luxury. Brands blaming weak demand need a better excuse.
editorialTake:
Swiss watch exports rose 9.1% in October, their fifth consecutive month of growth. Watches and jewellery showed strength while Gucci's sales decline deepened.

Gucci cut prices on selected products and added cheaper bags as its turnaround faced pressure. Those changes followed a worsening sales decline in the third quarter.

For jewellery businesses, Gucci's performance offers a limited guide to demand for their own products. Watch exports measure shipments, rather than purchases by shoppers, but jewellery sales provide separate evidence of spending. Richemont reported strong first-half sales across its jewellery brands.

readOneThing.title: Visa, Mastercard urge approval of $38 billion swipe fee settlement

items.title: Visa, Mastercard urge approval of $38 billion swipe fee settlement
bullets: US Judge Brian Cogan deferred a ruling on Visa and Mastercard's $38 billion merchant settlement in the 21-year-old antitrust case.
The agreement would cut card processing fees by 0.1 percentage point for five years and let merchants reject certain card categories.
The court received more than 1,000 objections, including from Walmart and the National Retail Federation, over fees and competition.
items.summary: Visa and Mastercard urged approval for a $38 billion swipe fee settlement that would cap fees on standard consumer cards.

items.title: Data breaches hit Muji, Chow Sang Sang and Sogo
bullets: Sogo reported unauthorised access to its membership system that may have exposed personal information belonging to 820,000 members in Hong Kong.
Muji operator Ryohin Keikaku said up to 27.26 million customer records were at risk, including credit card information associated with 1.09 million Muji Card records.
Chow Sang Sang detected unauthorised access to its membership and online shopping systems on November 9, potentially exposing customer and employee information.
items.summary: Data breaches at Muji, Chow Sang Sang and Sogo may have exposed millions of customer records.

items.title: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX
bullets: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share Wednesday, ahead of its planned Nasdaq debut Thursday under the symbol ANT.
Anthropic reported $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended September 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period in 2025.
Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices agreed to invest a combined $26 billion in Anthropic at the offering price.
items.summary: Anthropic raised over $81 billion in the largest initial public offering on record, topping SpaceX.

items.title: Gucci reportedly cuts prices as turnaround pressure builds
bullets: Gucci reportedly introduced unannounced summer price cuts, reducing its small Padlock handbag from €3,500 to €2,450 in France.
Gucci reported third-quarter revenue of €1.291 billion, down 4%, while sales through its own stores fell 9%.
Kering abandoned its goal of returning to growth in 2026 and increased planned net store closures to at least 125.
items.summary: Gucci cut prices on selected products and added cheaper bags as its sales decline deepened in the third quarter.

items.title: Strong ecommerce and ad sales drive Walmart's Q3 revenue growth and guidance upgrade
bullets: Walmart raised its fiscal 2027 net sales growth forecast to between 4.9% and 5.2%, excluding currency changes.
Walmart’s global online sales increased 17% year over year, with US online sales rising 23% during the quarter.
For the quarter ended October 31, Walmart’s net income fell 19.5% to $4.95 billion, primarily because of investment losses.
items.summary: Walmart raised its full-year forecast after third-quarter revenue rose 5.2% to $188.84 billion, helped by online sales and advertising.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower API prices and some benchmark gains
bullets: OpenAI made GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol available in ChatGPT Work and Codex, with Astra targeting professional work and Sol everyday tasks.
Astra’s API costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, 20 percent below its predecessor’s pricing.
Artificial Analysis placed Astra second in its Intelligence Index with 62 points, behind Claude Fable 5.2 at 65 points.
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol at lower API prices than their predecessors, with Astra ranking second on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

items.title: An F.P. Journe Becomes the Most Expensive Watch Ever Sold at Auction in France, Because Of Course
bullets: An F.P. Journe Tourbillon Souverain sold for €10.06 million at Bonhams in Paris on November 19, far above estimates.
The watch, made around 1999, was the seventh of 20 platinum examples and had never previously appeared at auction.
F.P. Journe Americas manager Pierre Halimi has criticized soaring auction prices, saying they attract buyers interested only in investment value.
items.summary: An F.P. Journe Tourbillon Souverain Souscription sold for $11.03 million at Bonhams Paris, setting France’s watch auction record.

items.title: Alibaba’s quick commerce gains as e-commerce slows
bullets: Alibaba reported a 10% increase in September-quarter revenue to US$40.5 billion, with growth from faster delivery and AI cloud services.
Alibaba’s China on-demand delivery business increased revenue 22% year on year to RMB58.8 billion as investment continued in Taobao Instant Commerce.
Alibaba’s international online shopping revenue fell 8% to RMB25.7 billion, largely because EU customs changes reduced AliExpress revenue.
items.summary: Alibaba’s fast delivery business grew strongly, offsetting falling revenue in its China and international online retail operations.
